title: Population and migration statistics transformation, Ceredigion case study: 2023
meta_description: Understanding the effectiveness of our administrative data in telling the story of Ceredigion.

breadcrumb.text: Population and migration statistics transformation, Ceredigion case study

lede: Understanding the effectiveness of our administrative data in telling the story of Ceredigion.

body.text: 27 June 2023
Ceredigion is a rural area with a small population, largely characterised by its high proportion of students.

This brings challenges when estimating the population at a given time, meaning more timely and granular data are needed to provide the most accurate picture of Ceredigion’s population and best direct services to meet needs across the area. This article shows how we can use administrative data alongside a wider range of data sources to achieve this.

All admin-based statistics in this article are referenced to mid-year, and Census 2021 statistics are referenced to March 2021. This may lead to some differences in the comparisons. The exception to this is the admin-based population estimates (ABPEs) (excluding Figure 3), which are compared with the Census 2021-based mid-year estimates.

Some statistics in this report are not official and should not be used for decision-making. They are estimates based on new methodologies that are different from those currently used to produce official statistics. These outputs must not be reproduced without this warning.

body.h3: Population and migration in Ceredigion
body.text: Population and migration in Ceredigion

body.h3: Population and migration in Ceredigion
body.text: The size and structure of the population in Ceredigion is largely characterised as a relatively stable population, with a large proportion of students. These patterns are similar for admin-based population estimates (ABPEs) and census-based mid-year estimates (MYEs). Our ABPEs show that there were 70,600 people living in Ceredigion in 2021. This increased by 0.9% to 71,300 in 2022 (Figure 2). The population was 51.2% female and 48.8% male.

body.h3: Population and migration in Ceredigion
body.h4: Notes:
body.text: We have compared our ABPEs with Census 2021 estimates at LSOA level. Approximately 85% of LSOAs show differences of within plus or minus 8% of the census estimates. There are greater differences between estimates than at local authority (LA) level in certain areas.

body.h3: Population and migration in Ceredigion
body.h4: Notes:
body.text: Our previous research shows these larger differences are often where there are communal establishments (CEs) with large, regularly changing populations, concentrated in small areas, such as students in halls of residence or armed forces in military bases. These population groups are less likely to interact with services in a typical way and may not be captured at the same location as the census.

body.h3: Population and migration in Ceredigion
body.h4: Notes:
body.text: Additionally, there are differences between census-based and admin-based estimates in areas with high levels of migration into and out of an area. This is because of differences in the reference period and the time taken to update administrative records following a move.

body.h3: Population sub-groups and characteristics in Ceredigion
body.text: Population sub-groups and characteristics in Ceredigion

body.h3: Population sub-groups and characteristics in Ceredigion
body.text: Beyond the size and structure of the population, we can learn more about the make-up of the local areas and communities across Ceredigion by examining the characteristics of those who live there. This will aid us in further understanding where inequalities may exist across the local areas in order to identify where additional support or services may be required.

body.h3: Population sub-groups and characteristics in Ceredigion
body.text: Ceredigion has a slightly higher proportion of people in the “White” ethnic group compared with Wales’s average (2.0 percentage points higher) in the [admin-based ethnicity statistics (ABES)](https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/culturalidentity/ethnicity/articles/developingadminbasedethnicitystatisticsforenglandandwales/2020). Conversely, for the “Asian”, “Black”, “Mixed” and “Other” ethnic groups, the figures for Ceredigion are up to 1.1 percentage points lower than the Welsh average.

body.h3: Population sub-groups and characteristics in Ceredigion
body.text: In comparison with Census 2021 figures, the ABES distributions for Ceredigion are broadly similar, but with some differences, notably for the “Asian” working-age population (Figure 5b). To some extent, this is because the ethnic minority population (excluding “White” ethnic minorities when we are referring to ethnic minority group) of Ceredigion is small. However, the ABES does underestimate the ethnic-minority populations by up to 0.4 percentage points. We noted similar patterns in our previous [Developing admin-based ethnicity statistics for England and Wales: 2020 article](https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/culturalidentity/ethnicity/articles/developingadminbasedethnicitystatisticsforenglandandwales/2020#ethnic-breakdown:~:text=Comparisons%20of%20ethnicity%20statistics).

body.h3: Housing, housing characteristics and living arrangements in Ceredigion
body.text: Housing, housing characteristics and living arrangements in Ceredigion

body.h3: Housing, housing characteristics and living arrangements in Ceredigion
body.text: Looking beyond the individuals who make up our population, we have used administrative data to understand how people live together across local communities.

body.h3: Housing, housing characteristics and living arrangements in Ceredigion
body.text: The census groups usual residents into households based on the self-reported use of shared facilities. Most residential addresses in England and Wales are used by a single household. In contrast, we report on occupied addresses because it is currently not possible to accurately identify multiple households at an address from administrative data alone. Addresses are most closely related to a self-contained dwelling definition. From the census, we estimate that this difference in definitions affects less than 1% of dwellings.

body.h3: Housing, housing characteristics and living arrangements in Ceredigion
body.text: Our admin-based occupied address dataset (ABOAD) identified 27,300 occupied addresses in Ceredigion in 2021, compared with 30,900 households in Census 2021. ABOAD counts occupied addresses while census counts households, so multiple households living at the same address will be counted individually for the census. This is not the only factor contributing to the difference, for example we have undercount in our underlying dataset and the base population, and these factors are likely to vary across geographies. For more information, please see our [technical topic guide](https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/populationandmigration/internationalmigration/methodologies/populationandmigrationstatisticstransformationinenglandandwalestechnicaltopicguide2023).

body.text: In Ceredigion, there are differences in the types of accommodation occupied by different ethnic groups, which are also reflected in the number of bedrooms.

body.text: Figure 12 shows that detached houses are the most common accommodation type for all ethnic groups, with almost half of Ceredigion’s population living in them. Compared with other ethnic groups, “White” individuals are most likely to live in detached houses, “Black” individuals are most likely to live in semi-detached houses, and those in the “Other” ethnic group are most likely to live in terraced houses.

body.h3: Housing, housing characteristics and living arrangements in Ceredigion
body.h4: Notes:
body.text: Beyond the population living in private households, we can learn more about the population living in communal establishments (CEs). CEs are places with full or part-time supervision providing accommodation. These groups are challenging to capture in our population, so work has started to understand more about who is living there. With more frequently updated figures, we can capture how the population living in CEs changes over time and the impact this has on the service provision for local areas.

body.h3: Housing, housing characteristics and living arrangements in Ceredigion
body.h4: Notes:
body.text: The admin-based communal establishment dataset (ABCED) shows that the total population living in CEs in Ceredigion was 3,345 compared with 3,630 on Census 2021. Of those found in CEs on administrative data, 85.7% lived in halls of residence.
